transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and guilt. I'm basically tense all day, just... waiting for something else to go wrong. And I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened. It's just kind of always there, and I need some help figuring it out.
Can you tell me about the specific event or situation that happened, that you feel you should have stopped?

Well, it was about four months ago. We were doing a porch repair, and... my husband fell. I just keep thinking I should have seen the danger and stopped it from happening. So, this has all been going on for four months, ever since that day.
Since the accident, have you been having unwanted, intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about your husband's fall?

Yeah, I have. It mostly happens when I'm at work. I'll just be... measuring a railing, or maybe I'll just hear a ladder scrape against a wall, and out of nowhere I can see him falling. It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just completely drops, and my hands get really shaky. So, yeah, I definitely get those memories when I don't want them.
Have you noticed yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or reminders—like ladders, heights, or home repair tasks—since your husband's fall?

Yeah, I have. At work, I've actually started turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or... or second-story decks. I just pass them on to someone else. And at home, it's kind of the same thing. I find excuses not to talk about the repair at all, and I really don't even look at the spot where it happened. I just try to avoid it completely.
Did these distressing memories and avoidance behaviors start right after your husband's fall, or did they begin sometime later, after a period where you felt relatively okay?

I'm not really sure. I don't remember a period after the accident where I felt okay, so... I think it pretty much started right after he fell. If there was a delay before all this started happening, I didn't really notice it.
Since the accident, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, or having trouble sleeping or concentrating?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty bad. Most nights, I just lie there in bed for an hour or two... replaying everything that happened. And even when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I don't stay asleep. I wake up at every little creak the house makes. Or I wake up from these dreams where... where I hear the sound of him hitting the ground again. So, yeah, sleeping has been really tough.
